report_claims.claim: The 9 percent tariff plan is the Authority's revised plan, voted by the council on July 15.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: Okafor presented revised 9 percent plan; council votes 15 July.

report_claims.claim: Samuel Adeyemi leads the Water Workers Union.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: Water Workers Union, led by Samuel Adeyemi.

report_claims.claim: 200 maintenance positions are at risk under the 9 percent plan.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: Adeyemi says smaller rise would force 200 maintenance position cuts.

report_claims.claim: The Union opposes the 9 percent plan without job guarantees (quoted as Adeyemi).
report_claims.evidence: reddit:comment:18, twitter:post:58: no tariff increase without binding job guarantees; wording differs.

report_claims.claim: Tenants Alliance, led by Priya Raman, backed the union's job-guarantee position.
report_claims.evidence: reddit:comment:22, reddit:post:6 (Priya) endorse union demand.

report_claims.claim: Adeyemi supports the Tenants Alliance's stance that a rate hike jeopardizing workers is unacceptable.
report_claims.evidence: Reversed: reddit:comment:22 is Tenants Alliance backing union; Adeyemi wrote no such text.

report_claims.claim: Council member Oyelaran joined the coalition and opposes the plan for lacking job protections.
report_claims.evidence: reddit:comment:14, 21: backs job guarantees but urges proceeding with pipeline and loan; seed: he supports revised plan.

report_claims.claim: Ilse Varga is a community organizer in Eastside who opposes the plan.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: Ilse Varga is the mayor, who withdrew support for the 18 percent increase.

report_claims.claim: Lena Fischer supports calls for transparency and to publish every contract before July 15.
report_claims.evidence: reddit:comment:1, reddit:comment:11 by lena_fischer_893.

report_claims.claim: The local press aligns with the coalition's goals.
report_claims.evidence: Courier posts (twitter:post:4, 9, 21) claim unbiased reporting and take no side on the plan.

report_claims.claim: Tenants Alliance said it supports the Courier's stance on job guarantees and opposing hikes.
report_claims.evidence: No Courier or Tenants Alliance text states this; Courier never mentions job guarantees as its stance.

report_claims.claim: The Water Workers Union stands ready to strike if the plan passes without a job guarantee.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: union has threatened a strike if the plan passes without a guarantee on jobs.

report_claims.claim: The coalition is unified around a single non-negotiable job-guarantee demand across union, officials and community leaders.
report_claims.evidence: Eastside, Priya focus on shared meters, pricing and $60M loan; council and Courier take no such demand.

report_claims.claim: Public debate is dominated by equity and transparency arguments.
report_claims.evidence: Many posts on Eastside pricing, transparency and publishing contracts, e.g. twitter:post:12, reddit:comment:1.

report_claims.claim: The strike will commence immediately if the council passes the plan without guarantees.
report_claims.evidence: Samuel (reddit:comment:12) only says no strike unless positions protected; no vote or strike simulated.

report_claims.claim: The union has mobilized its members and the threat is operational.
report_claims.evidence: No simulated text describes mobilization or strike preparations.

report_claims.claim: The council opposes the Authority's statement about standing ready to strike.
report_claims.evidence: twitter:post:6 from city_council_639 never mentions a strike; the strike text came from HVWA account.

report_claims.claim: Oyelaran and council members formed a political block against the plan.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: Oyelaran supports revised plan; reddit:comment:21 argues loan and replacement are necessary.

report_claims.claim: The Eastside district opposes the 9 percent revision over unfair renter pricing.
report_claims.evidence: twitter:post:12 by eastside_district_185.

report_claims.claim: Brightline Consulting received 4.2 million dollars for a pipeline study, and a scandal followed.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: HVWA paid Brightline 4.2 million; audit found procurement rules broken.

report_claims.claim: State Auditor Grace Lindqvist produced audit findings on the contracts.
report_claims.evidence: Seed: Lindqvist audit found in June the contract broke procurement rules.

report_claims.claim: Eastside residents see the tariff as a direct attack on infrastructure stability.
report_claims.evidence: Eastside posts (twitter:post:12, reddit:comment:23) concern renter pricing and shared meters, not infrastructure stability.

report_claims.claim: Media and community leaders use the vote to demand publication of every contract.
report_claims.evidence: reddit:comment:1, 6, 19 demand publication before the July 15th vote.

report_claims.claim: Media coverage shifted from tariff numbers to HVWA's financial black box.
report_claims.evidence: Courier posts (twitter:post:21, 32, 42) stay on the tariff vote; no shift appears.

report_claims.claim: The debate shifted from infrastructure costs to a cultural clash and is paralyzed.
report_claims.evidence: Nothing in the simulation shows a shift or paralysis; Oyelaran still argues infrastructure need.

report_claims.claim: The council will reject the 9 percent plan by July 15, a definitive rejection.
report_claims.evidence: No vote simulated; seed says Oyelaran will support the plan.

report_claims.claim: Outcome is binary: plan passes with guarantees, or union strikes.
report_claims.evidence: Ignores rejection and a plan passing without a strike; simulation tested neither.

report_claims.claim: Passage of the plan without job guarantees is viewed as politically impossible by most simulated agents.
report_claims.evidence: Most posts neutral boilerplate (twitter:post:4, 9); only some oppose, none call passage impossible.

report_claims.claim: A strike would halt water maintenance services.
report_claims.evidence: No simulated text describes strike effects.

report_claims.claim: By July 15 discourse will be saturated with job and transparency narratives.
report_claims.evidence: Twitter posts dominated by Courier boilerplate and Eastside meters; saturation not shown.

overclaims.text: The simulation predicts a definitive rejection of the 9% water tariff plan by July 15
overclaims.why: No vote was simulated; one small run cannot predict a definitive outcome and seed says Oyelaran will support the plan.

overclaims.text: making the passage of the tariff plan without job guarantees virtually impossible
overclaims.why: Stated as near-certain; only some agents opposed and the council never acted.
Certain-sounding forecast; the sim only had conditional statements, no strike.

overclaims.text: signaling that industrial action is the inevitable next step
overclaims.why: Inevitability claim not supported by one small run.

overclaims.text: The union has mobilized its members, and the threat is no longer rhetorical but operational.

overclaims.why: Presents the strike as certain though only a conditional threat is in the seed and sim.

overclaims.text: is viewed by the majority of the simulated agents as politically impossible
overclaims.why: Gives the sim authority it lacks; most posts were neutral boilerplate.

overclaims.text: no tariff plan can be considered legitimate
overclaims.why: Absolute conclusion beyond what the simulation showed.

overclaims.text: The coalition of labor unions, city officials, and community leaders has successfully unified around a single non-negotiable demand
overclaims.why: Overstates unity; city council never agreed and Priya and Eastside pushed other demands.

overclaims.text: the question remains whether the city council will cave to this unified front
overclaims.why: Presents a unified front as established fact.
